title: Housing pledge approved with calls on province
subtitle: Also: Elliott long-term care expansion funding, operations facilities plan, organics contract, Greener Homes authority and Integrity Commissioner report.
overview: Council approved the City of Guelph Housing Pledge to facilitate 18,000 homes by 2031 {{vote:m16}}. The pledge was amended several times to state that meeting the target depends on provincial action. It also asks the Province for brownfield clean-up investment, surplus provincial land for non-profit housing, more affordable and accessible housing funding, a five-year freeze on target changes, and funding of the third-party audit program. Copies are to go to federal representatives too. Staff said the pledge helps the city's case for infrastructure funding.

Council approved The Elliott's 29-bed long-term care expansion, including a one-time capital contribution of $862,780 and interim financing of up to $6.2 million {{vote:m17}}. It made the project contingent on hiring a certified project manager, with monthly updates {{vote:m18}}.

Council also renewed the organics processing agreement with the Region of Waterloo through 2028 with the price index suspended {{vote:m3}}. It endorsed the operations facilities plan and asked for an information report on costs before the multi-year budget {{vote:m7}}. After closed session, the Mayor reported that Council gave staff direction on firefighter bargaining and received information on 70 Fountain Street East.

decisions.detail: Council approved the pledge for 18,000 units by 2031, as amended, and authorized the Mayor to submit it to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing.
Council called on the Province to freeze population targets and time horizons for five years and stop changing the Planning Act {{vote:m12}}.
Council approved Phases 1 and 2 of the 29-bed expansion, a one-time $862,780 contribution, and interim financing of up to $6.2 million.
Approval is contingent on hiring a certified Project Management Professional, and Elliott staff must give monthly updates to the Committee of Management.
Council renewed the Region of Waterloo agreement from October 14, 2023 to October 13, 2028 and suspended the annual price index adjustment.
Staff will keep designing a new transit and fleet facility at Watson Parkway and Stone Road and revise the plan for existing municipal sites, seeking approval through the multi-year budget.
Staff must provide an information report on anticipated costs and a revised timeline before the multi-year budget process.
Council delegated authority to sign Greener Homes Program agreements to the Deputy CAO and, for property owner agreements, to the City Clerk and responsible manager.

debate: Staff and a guest economist said the 18,000-unit target is roughly double recent building rates, and that labour shortages, interest rates and reduced development charges are outside the city's control.

A delegate asked Council to pause the pledge over a new report suggesting existing capacity exceeds the provincial target. Another delegate called the pledge unrealistic and one-sided. A councillor asked how that report squares with Guelph's low vacancy rate.

A home builders' association delegate supported most of the pledge. The association opposed exempting secondary plan appeals and holding builders jointly accountable for targets. It asked for lower parking minimums and an urban boundary expansion. Councillors asked about approved but unbuilt units and building capacity.

On the five-year freeze, one councillor said the Province, not the city, sets population targets and municipalities need time to implement their plans. Another councillor worried that it wades into immigration policy.

On the operations facilities plan, a trail club delegate asked for integrated trail planning. Staff said trails are already part of the work. A councillor asked for an information report so Council keeps sight of costs before budget, while others cautioned against debating preliminary figures.
